title: IAM schema migrations at service boot
name: Identity schema migrator

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies and records IAM schema migrations? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Migration 42 runs against a table that has two bindings with the same principal, role and scope, ids 10 and 17. What happens?
choices: The constraint creation fails because of the duplicate
Both rows are deleted, then the constraint is added
Row 17 is deleted, row 10 is kept, and the constraint is added
Row 10 is deleted, row 17 is kept, and the constraint is added

questions.prompt: Three replicas of the identity service boot at once with migrations 41-43 pending. How do they interact?
choices: All three run 41 at once and two fail on ALTER TABLE
One acquires the advisory lock and applies them; the others wait, then see max(version)=43 and apply nothing
The first to boot applies them; the others exit because the lock is held

questions.prompt: While migration 41 runs on a large role_bindings table, what does it mean for authorization checks reading that table?
choices: They are unaffected because ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN takes no lock
They block until the migration's transaction commits, because ALTER TABLE holds an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the whole transaction including the full-table UPDATE
They see scope = NULL for some rows until the transaction commits
They fail immediately with a lock timeout
